metadata.description: Biological and NGS library prep interpretations for fastp QC metrics. Each variable contains flag logic, causes, and severity guidance for high and low deviations.

read1_total_reads_retention.description: Percentage of Read1 reads retained after QC filtering

low.short_summary: Read1 retention below expected threshold — significant read loss after QC.
biological_causes: DNA degradation producing short or damaged fragments in DNA-seq
FFPE DNA damage causing widespread base-level errors
Low-quality input material with high percentage of compromised molecules
library_prep_causes: Short-insert library with read-through into adapter sequence
Failed size-selection step retaining excess short fragments
Under-ligation leaving excess unligated adapters
PCR over-amplification generating low-complexity or chimeric reads
sequencing_causes: Tile-level flowcell failure degrading a portion of Read1 clusters
Over-clustering causing signal bleed and increased base call errors
Reagent degradation mid-run causing late-cycle quality collapse
low.recommended_action: Check read1 length distribution and filter category breakdown. Cross-reference with too_short_reads and low_quality_reads counts. Inspect flowcell tile quality maps if available.

read2_total_reads_retention.description: Percentage of Read2 reads retained after QC filtering

low.short_summary: Read2 retention below expected threshold — significant read loss after QC.
biological_causes: DNA degradation particularly affecting the anti-sense strand in stranded DNA-seq
FFPE-induced deamination producing C-to-T errors concentrated in later cycles
Low-integrity sample with fragmented nucleic acids
library_prep_causes: Short-insert library causing R2 read-through into R1 adapter sequence
Random hexamer priming artifacts creating truncated R2 reads
Strand-switching protocol issues (e.g. SMART-seq) degrading the second strand in certain cases or types
Asymmetric adapter ligation efficiency affecting R2 mate
sequencing_causes: R2 is sequenced after more cycles have elapsed — inherently higher quality decay
Phasing and pre-phasing errors accumulate more in R2
Platform-specific R2 signal degradation in later sequencing cycles
low.recommended_action: Compare R1 vs R2 retention to assess asymmetry. High asymmetry with R2 lower than R1 is expected in paired-end runs but extreme values warrant investigation. Check insert size distribution.

total_q30_before_after_comp.description: Relative change in Q30 rate after QC filtering: (after - before) / after * 100. Positive = improvement after filtering.

high.short_summary: Large Q30 improvement after QC — many low-quality bases removed, suggesting problematic raw data.
biological_causes: High GC content causing signal imbalance and base-call uncertainty
Repetitive genomic regions producing ambiguous cluster signals
DNA degradation introducing misincorporations across many reads
library_prep_causes: Low-complexity library producing phasing errors that inflate low-quality bases
PCR artifacts generating reads with systematic base-call errors
Adapter dimers with poor quality scores enriched in the raw data
sequencing_causes: Systematic chemistry degradation disproportionately affecting raw quality
Over-clustering causing signal bleed and widespread quality reduction
Tile or swath failures pulling down quality in a subset of clusters
Expired or degraded sequencing reagents
high.recommended_action: Investigate raw Q30 values and compare to cohort baseline. High delta indicates raw data was substantially below standard — check run metrics and reagent logs.

low.short_summary: Q30 rate unchanged or marginally changed after QC — raw quality was already high or filtering had minimal effect.
biological_causes: High-quality input material with minimal base-level damage
Simple, low-GC genome or target region producing clean signal
library_prep_causes: Clean high-complexity library with minimal adapter contamination
Optimal PCR cycle count preserving base-call fidelity
sequencing_causes: Excellent run chemistry and cluster density
Could also indicate QC trimming thresholds were too permissive
low.recommended_action: Verify QC parameters were applied correctly. Near-zero Q30 delta is expected in clean runs but confirm filtering was not inadvertently skipped.

normal.short_summary: Q30 before/after comparison within expected range.

total_q20_before_after_comp.description: Relative change in Q20 rate after QC filtering: (after - before) / after * 100. Positive = improvement after filtering.

high.short_summary: Large Q20 improvement after QC — raw quality substantially compromised across many reads.
biological_causes: Severely degraded DNA or RNA (RIN < 5 or DIN < 3)
FFPE oxidation damage (8-oxoguanine causing G-to-T transversions)
High proportion of damaged template molecules in the input
library_prep_causes: Contaminating inhibitors from sample extraction affecting polymerase fidelity
Excessive PCR cycles generating error-prone amplicons
Low-input library requiring aggressive amplification
sequencing_causes: Severe run failure or chemistry collapse
Long read cycles with rapid quality decay beyond cycle 100
Low-complexity library causing widespread cluster mis-assignment
high.recommended_action: A high Q20 delta with high Q30 delta together confirm global quality failure in the raw run. Check if Q20 delta exceeds Q30 delta — if so, mid-quality bases are preferentially being removed suggesting a specific quality tier of damage.

low.short_summary: Q20 rate unchanged or marginally changed after QC.
biological_causes: High-quality input with minimal damage
library_prep_causes: Clean library preparation with adequate input material
sequencing_causes: Good run quality with no significant error-rate inflation
Possible under-trimming if other metrics show quality issues
low.recommended_action: Near-zero Q20 delta is expected in clean runs. If Q30 delta is also low, overall run quality was good. If Q30 delta is high but Q20 is low, consider whether trimming was asymmetric.

normal.short_summary: Q20 before/after comparison within expected range.

total_gc_before_after_comp.description: Relative change in GC content after QC filtering: (before - after) / before * 100. Positive = GC content decreased after filtering.

high.short_summary: GC content shifted substantially after QC — filtered reads had different GC composition than retained reads.
biological_causes: GC-rich adapter dimers or contamination preferentially removed by length/quality filters
Organismal contamination with distinct GC profile being removed
library_prep_causes: PCR GC bias amplifying GC-rich fragments that are then quality-filtered
Adapter dimer enrichment in GC-rich ligation junctions removed by short-read filter
Nextera/Tn5 transposase GC insertion bias creating a filterable GC-rich population
sequencing_causes: GC-rich reads from high-complexity regions collapsing to lower quality and being removed
GC content imbalance causing signal suppression in high-GC clusters
high.recommended_action: Cross-reference with adapter_trimmed_reads_percentage and too_short_reads. High GC shift with high adapter trimming suggests GC-rich adapter dimers. Plot GC distribution before/after to identify the shifted population.

low.short_summary: GC content stable before and after QC — filtering did not selectively remove GC-biased reads.
biological_causes: Uniform GC distribution across all reads including those filtered
AT-rich genome where quality filtering is GC-neutral
library_prep_causes: Balanced library with no GC-related enrichment artifact
Enzymatic fragmentation producing GC-neutral fragments
sequencing_causes: Consistent signal across GC content range — well-balanced chemistry
low.recommended_action: Low GC shift is the expected outcome in a clean library. No action required unless GC deviation from expected species GC is observed in absolute values.

normal.short_summary: GC before/after comparison within expected range.

total_reads_before_after_comp.description: Percentage of reads lost during QC: (before - after) / before * 100.

high.short_summary: Large proportion of reads removed during QC — significant read attrition.
biological_causes: Degraded RNA/DNA producing short or damaged reads that fail quality or length filters
FFPE-induced damage causing widespread quality failures
High proportion of contaminating sequences (non-target organism)
library_prep_causes: Excess adapter dimers inflating total reads but being filtered as too-short
Over-amplification producing low-quality chimeric reads
Incorrect adapter sequence specified — reads not trimmed before quality filtering
sequencing_causes: PhiX or internal control reads counted and then filtered
Index hopping producing mis-assigned reads that fail barcode quality
high.recommended_action: Decompose the loss into filter categories: too_short, low_quality, too_many_N. High reads loss dominated by too_short suggests adapter/fragment-size issues; dominated by low_quality suggests run chemistry failure.

low.short_summary: Minimal read loss during QC — high-quality library.
biological_causes: Clean, high-integrity input material
library_prep_causes: Optimal fragment size and adapter ligation — minimal trimming needed
sequencing_causes: Good run quality — low error rate across all clusters
low.recommended_action: Near-zero reads loss is ideal. Confirm QC was correctly applied if value is 0.00 — may indicate filtering step was skipped.

normal.short_summary: Total reads before/after comparison within expected range.

total_bases_before_after_comp.description: Percentage of bases lost during QC: (before - after) / before * 100. Higher than reads loss because trimming also removes bases from retained reads.

high.short_summary: Large proportion of bases removed during QC — significant trimming or read filtering occurred.
biological_causes: DNA degradation shortening fragments and reducing usable base yield
Short-insert library where read-through into adapter wastes sequencing bases
Heavily damaged FFPE material with high per-base error rate requiring hard trimming
library_prep_causes: Aggressive adapter trimming of short-insert libraries
Incorrect insert-size selection leaving many short fragments
High adapter dimer content consuming sequencing capacity
sequencing_causes: 3-prime quality decay requiring hard clipping of read tails
Extended read length beyond insert size — all excess bases trimmed
high.recommended_action: Compare bases loss to reads loss. If bases loss >> reads loss, trimming is removing bases from many retained reads (quality or adapter trimming). If similar, entire reads are being removed. Both insert size and read length loss metrics should be reviewed together.

biological_causes: High-quality input with minimal base-level damage
library_prep_causes: Long inserts relative to read length — minimal adapter read-through
sequencing_causes: Low error rate — minimal quality-based trimming needed
low.recommended_action: Expected in clean, long-insert libraries. Verify trimming was applied if this is unexpectedly low given other quality metrics.

normal.short_summary: Total bases before/after comparison within expected range.

duplication_rate.description: Percentage of reads identified as PCR or optical duplicates.

high.short_summary: Duplication rate exceeds expected threshold — possible low library complexity or over-amplification.
biological_causes: Low-complexity target region (narrow ChIP-seq peaks, amplicon sequencing)
Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from plasma — inherently limited diversity
Small input cell number limiting unique molecule diversity
Biologically repetitive genomic regions
library_prep_causes: Insufficient input material requiring excessive PCR cycles (< 1 ng DNA)
Failed or inefficient size selection reducing library diversity
Carry-over contamination from a previous high-duplication library
UMI-tagged library where UMIs were not collapsed before fastp duplication assessment
sequencing_causes: Optical duplicates elevated by high patterned flowcell cluster density
ExAmp clustering artefacts generating optical duplicate clusters
high.recommended_action: Cross-reference with insert_size and low_quality_reads. High duplication + normal insert size suggests PCR over-amplification. High duplication + short insert size suggests low-complexity or degraded input. For ChIP/ATAC samples, use assay-specific duplication benchmarks, not WGS standards.

low_quality_reads.description: Number of reads removed due to failing minimum quality score threshold.

high.short_summary: Elevated low-quality read count — substantial fraction of sequencing data unusable.
biological_causes: Heavily degraded input RNA/DNA with widespread base-level damage
FFPE sample with extensive deamination and oxidation
Samples with high inhibitor content affecting base-call signal quality
library_prep_causes: Low-input library with over-amplification generating high-error reads
Contaminated library with nucleases or inhibitors from extraction
PCR chimerism producing reads with systematic base errors
sequencing_causes: Flowcell chemistry failure or tile-level dropout causing widespread quality collapse
Reagent degradation mid-run causing late-cycle quality crash
Over-clustering causing signal bleed inflating per-base error rates
Index hopping producing mis-assigned reads with poor quality scores
high.recommended_action: High low_quality_reads is a critical flag. Examine run-level quality metrics (Q30 trends per cycle). If spatially clustered in flowcell tiles, the run has a physical failure. If uniform across tiles, input material or chemistry is the likely cause. Consider re-sequencing.

normal.short_summary: Low quality read count within acceptable range.

too_many_N_reads.description: Number of reads removed because they exceeded the maximum allowed N (undetermined base) count.

high.short_summary: Elevated undetermined base (N) read count — basecaller unable to assign bases in many reads.
biological_causes: Extreme GC content causing signal collapse and N calling in affected regions
Strong RNA/DNA secondary structure blocking polymerase and collapsing signal
Highly repetitive regions producing ambiguous cluster signals
library_prep_causes: Very short insert library with reads extending entirely past the insert into adapter
Adapter dimer population that reads as poly-N after the insert
Ligation failure producing reads with no insert — reads collapse to primer sequence only
sequencing_causes: Choked cluster — over-clustering causing signal interference and N calling
Tile-level failure where all clusters on affected tiles call N
Index hopping or de-multiplexing failure producing reads assigned to wrong sample with N bases
Phasing/pre-phasing accumulation in very long reads causing terminal N calling
high.recommended_action: Check spatial distribution of N reads on flowcell — tile-specific failures are run QC issues. If uniform, investigate insert size and GC content. Too_many_N_reads is particularly sensitive to flowcell tile failures.

normal.short_summary: Too-many-N read count within acceptable range.

too_short_reads.description: Number of reads removed because they fell below the minimum read length threshold after trimming.

high.short_summary: Elevated short read count — many reads trimmed below minimum length, indicating short-insert or degraded library.
biological_causes: DNA degradation producing short fragments that read through entirely into adapter
cfDNA from plasma — inherently short fragments (~167 bp mono-nucleosomal)
Heavily fragmented FFPE DNA with very short recoverable inserts
library_prep_causes: Over-fragmentation — excessive sonication time, too much enzyme, or over-tagmentation
Failed or suboptimal size selection allowing short fragments to pass
Adapter dimer population: ligated adapters with no insert — entirely trimmed away
Incorrect AMPure bead ratio enriching for short fragments
sequencing_causes: Read length longer than insert size by design — expected for short-insert protocols
Aggressive adapter trimming settings removing long tails and leaving sub-threshold reads
high.recommended_action: Cross-reference with insert_size and read1/read2_length_loss. High too_short_reads with short insert size is a library preparation issue. High too_short_reads with normal insert size suggests adapter contamination or aggressive trimming settings.

normal.short_summary: Too-short read count within acceptable range.

read1_length_loss.description: Percentage of Read1 mean length lost after QC trimming: (before - after) / before * 100.

high.short_summary: Significant Read1 length trimmed away — adapter contamination or 3-prime quality decay.
biological_causes: Short-insert library where R1 overshoots the insert and reads into the adapter
DNA degradation producing short fragments — reads extend past insert into adapter
cfDNA short fragments requiring heavy trimming
library_prep_causes: Insert size smaller than read length — inevitable adapter read-through
Failed size selection leaving excess short fragments
Transposase (Tn5/Nextera) tagmentation producing very short fragments
Incomplete adapter cleanup leaving ligated adapters on short fragments
sequencing_causes: 3-prime quality decay requiring hard clipping at the read tail
Aggressive quality trimming settings set below Phred 20 cutoff
high.recommended_action: Check insert_size alongside R1 length loss. If insert_size < read_length, some R1 length loss is expected. Disproportionate R1 loss vs R2 loss may indicate asymmetric adapter contamination or quality issues.

normal.short_summary: Read1 length loss within expected range.

read2_length_loss.description: Percentage of Read2 mean length lost after QC trimming: (before - after) / before * 100.

high.short_summary: Significant Read2 length trimmed away — short inserts causing R2 read-through or 3-prime quality decay.
biological_causes: Short-insert library — R2 reads through insert into R1 adapter or R1 itself
DNA degradation creating very short usable fragments
cfDNA mono-nucleosomal fragments (~167 bp) being read by R2 from the opposite end
library_prep_causes: Insert size smaller than read length — R2 reads through into R1 adapter sequence
Random hexamer priming artifacts creating truncated R2 reads in DNA-seq
Secondary structure in insert blocking extension of R2
sequencing_causes: R2 3-prime quality decay is inherently more severe than R1 — more cycles elapsed
Phasing accumulation reducing R2 signal quality in later cycles
high.recommended_action: R2 length loss is expected to be equal to or greater than R1 length loss in most protocols. If R2 >> R1, short insert or R2-specific quality issue. Compare with insert_size to determine if read-through is the cause.

normal.short_summary: Read2 length loss within expected range.

percentage_reads_survived.description: Percentage of total read pairs passing all QC filters.

low.short_summary: Overall read survival below threshold — compound QC failures reducing usable data substantially.
biological_causes: Degraded input material failing multiple filter categories simultaneously
High organismal contamination where contaminating reads fail all quality criteria
FFPE samples with widespread damage producing multi-category failures
library_prep_causes: Wrong adapter sequence specified — reads not trimmed, then fail quality filters
Excess adapter dimers counted as reads but filtered as too-short
Over-amplification generating chimeric reads that fail quality and length thresholds
sequencing_causes: Run-level failure causing compound quality, N, and length failures across many reads
Index hopping inflating raw read count with mis-assigned reads that then fail QC
low.recommended_action: Decompose survival loss into component filter categories. % reads survived is the product of all individual filter pass rates. Low survival driven by one dominant category is more diagnosable than uniform loss across all categories.

normal.short_summary: Read survival rate within expected range.

percentage_bases_survived.description: Percentage of total bases passing all QC filters (includes trimming within retained reads).

low.short_summary: Overall base survival below threshold — significant base loss through trimming and read filtering.
biological_causes: Degraded sample producing short fragments with heavy adapter contamination
Highly damaged FFPE material where read tails are universally low quality
library_prep_causes: Short-insert library — substantial fraction of each read is adapter sequence
Low-complexity library generating redundant bases that are not technically 'lost' but filtered as duplicates
Incorrect size selection leaving many short adapter-containing fragments
sequencing_causes: 3-prime quality decay requiring extensive tail clipping on most reads
Long read cycles beyond insert end — all overhang bases trimmed
low.recommended_action: Compare with percentage_reads_survived. If bases survived << reads survived, trimming is the dominant mechanism (bases removed from retained reads). If approximately equal, entire reads are being removed. Both signals require different corrective actions.

normal.short_summary: Base survival rate within expected range.

insert_size.description: Peak insert size estimated by fastp from fragment analysis.

low.short_summary: Insert size below expected range — library is over-fragmented or input was degraded.
biological_causes: DNA degradation producing short cDNA inserts in DNA-seq
cfDNA libraries where short mono-nucleosomal fragments are biologically expected (~167 bp)
FFPE-induced DNA fragmentation limiting recoverable fragment length
library_prep_causes: Over-sonication or excessive enzymatic fragmentation of DNA
Tn5 transposase over-activity in ATAC-seq or Nextera XT libraries
Insufficient enzyme inactivation or cleanup allowing continued fragmentation
AMPure bead ratio too high — selecting only very short fragments
Contaminating nuclease activity in sample or reagents
sequencing_causes: Short insert directly increases adapter read-through frequency
Increased too_short_reads and read length loss are downstream consequences
low.recommended_action: Short insert size is a primary library QC indicator. Cross-reference with too_short_reads, read1_length_loss, and duplication_rate. For cfDNA assays, low insert may be expected. For WGS/RNA-seq, short insert size indicates library prep optimisation is needed.

adapter_timmed_reads_percentage.description: Percentage of reads requiring adapter trimming: adapter_trimmed_reads / before_total_reads * 100.

high.short_summary: High proportion of reads required adapter trimming — short inserts causing widespread read-through.
biological_causes: DNA degradation producing short cDNA fragments that read through adapter in DNA-seq
cfDNA short mono-nucleosomal fragments inherently requiring adapter trimming
library_prep_causes: Insert size smaller than read length — all reads will require adapter trimming
Excess adapter dimer population: fully ligated adapters with no insert
Failed or insufficient size selection allowing all insert sizes through
Over-tagmentation (ATAC-seq) producing very short nucleosome-free region fragments
sequencing_causes: Read length set longer than library insert size — systematic read-through expected
Adapter contamination not removed during library cleanup steps
high.recommended_action: High adapter trimming % is strongly linked to insert_size. If insert_size < read_length, this is expected and the adapter trimming is functioning correctly. Concerning when paired with low survival rate, indicating trimmed reads are also failing length filters. Check too_short_reads count alongside adapter trimming.

normal.short_summary: Adapter trimmed reads percentage within expected range.
